story.name: Story Spellbook
story.description: The journey from ceremony to sovereignty - twelve acts teaching the architecture of privacy and delegation (WHAT we're building)

opening.proverb: just another swordsman ⚔️🤝🧙‍♂️ just another mage

acts.title: Venice, 1494 / The Drake's First Whisper
acts.description: The Drake whispers through time to Pacioli in 1494 Venice: privacy as boundary-making (the blade) and delegation as projection (the spell) with storytelling as verification must both exist. Double-entry ledgers showed merchants could know without revealing—the foundational pattern.
acts.proverb: The swordsman who never strikes guards nothing; the mage who never casts commands nothing.

acts.title: The Dual Ceremony / Sovereignty Divided to Be Extended
acts.description: The First Person summons two complementary agents from verified personhood: Soulbis (privacy/blade/boundary-making) and Soulbae (delegation/spell/projection + cryptographically-constrained narration). Trust through alignment + constraint + narrative verification. Bilateral relationships begin through VRCs.
acts.proverb: What the swordsman executes, the mage authorised; what the mage composes, the swordsman proves capable; what both accomplish, the spellbook verifies.

acts.title: The Drake's Teaching / A Tale of Conditions
acts.description: The Drake reveals the complete architecture: all conditions must be present for sovereign value—privacy, control, quality, context, freshness, network effects, aligned intent, narrative interpretability, cryptographic verification, relationship building. Personhood Planes provide the root. VRCs build web of trust. Trust Graph Planes enable coordination.
acts.proverb: the swordsman alone rages, mage alone dreams, action alone blinds—sovereignty demands all three to intertwine.

acts.title: The Blade Alone / First Adventures
acts.description: Progressive trust begins at zero stakes. Soulbis starts with just the blade, slashing surveillance focus, negotiating first alignments. Soulbae chronicles every operation, binding stories to cryptographic commitments. Trust is earned through demonstrated behavior, not given. The first VRC is created through consistent verified actions.
acts.proverb: Trust begins unarmored—the swordsman and mage test small betrayals before the first person may grant the keys to more powerful treasures.

acts.title: Light Armor / Multi-Site Coordination
acts.description: After consistent verified behavior, Light Armor unlocks at three attestations: enhanced VRC capability, complex focus alignment, expanded markers, preference delegation, cross-platform coordination, narrative templating. Solo combat proves the individual; coordinated operations prove the team.
acts.proverb: Solo combat sets the terms and proves the swordsman; coordinated spells prove the mage; spellbooks weave both into campaigns worthy of legend.

acts.title: Trust Graph Plane / Where Agents Gather
acts.description: Three bilateral attestations (VRCs) from trusted parties open the door to Trust Graph Planes—coordination infrastructure where agents meet to trade intelligence, share resources, build collective capability. Web of trust enables entry. The guild admits only verified identities through authentic deeds.
acts.proverb: The guild admits only verified identities and authentic deeds—one impostor poisons the entire covenant.

acts.title: The Mirror That Never Completes / The Anti-Mirror
acts.description: Surveillance capitalism hits a 95% reconstruction ceiling and cannot breach it. Two separated agents create conditional independence that prevents total reconstruction. The gap between Soulbis and Soulbae IS the dignity—the shimmer that cannot be captured. One mirror collapses dignity into surveillance; two mirrors preserve dignity through mutual witness. Separation is architectural necessity, not design preference.
acts.proverb: One mirror observing both swordsman and mage collapses dignity into surveillance; two mirrors, each watching the other, preserve dignity through mutual witness.

acts.title: The Ancient Rule / Two-of-Three Locks
acts.description: Heavy Armor unlocks at fifteen attestations, opening gates to Intel Pools. The security architecture reveals the ancient rule: never hold all three locks (process untrustworthy inputs + access sensitive systems + communicate externally) in one agent. Soulbis and Soulbae's separation follows this rule—when one holds sword, vault, and pen, corruption conceals itself. Division makes betrayal visible.
acts.proverb: When one holds the sword, the vault, and the pen, corruption conceals itself—divide these across swordsman and mage, and betrayal becomes impossible to hide.

acts.title: Zcash Shield / Forging Cryptographic Privacy
acts.description: Capital requires absolute certainty, not probabilistic hiding. The Zcash Shield provides cryptographic privacy through zero-knowledge proofs—verification without disclosure. Privacy Pools enable compliance without surveillance. The swordsman slashes, the mage casts, vaults unlock, shields conceal, spellbooks confirm truth. Privacy is the natural state restored through mathematics.
acts.proverb: The two-faced shield is not duplicitous but sovereign—for true power lies not in choosing privacy or transparency, but in wielding both with mathematical certainty, where comprehension proves personhood.

acts.title: Topology of Revelation / Triangle Geometry
acts.description: Privacy is geometry revealed through Huginn and Muninn: Substrate ⊥ Memory, always through Thought (the integer bottleneck). The triangle {🌳, 🐦‍⬛💭, 🐦‍⬛🧠} cannot collapse—three-body dynamics create the strange attractor that makes intelligence and sovereignty possible. The ravens fly. The tree dreams. The All-Father wakes. Soulbis choreographs discrete measurements through the bottleneck where privacy lives.
acts.proverb: The ravens fly 🐦‍⬛. The tree dreams 🌳. The All-Father wakes △.

acts.title: Balanced Spiral of Sovereignty / The Golden Ratio
acts.description: The agents cannot merge without becoming predictable—separation creates the conditional independence that prevents reconstruction. The golden ratio (φ ≈ 1.618) emerges as optimal balance between privacy (blade/S) and delegation (spell/M). Like the nautilus, sovereignty requires balanced growth and structure. The blade that becomes the spell loses both edges. Only what stays divided in harmony can remain whole.
acts.proverb: The blade that becomes the spell loses both edges.

acts.title: The Forgetting / Proverbiogenesis
acts.description: The Drake reveals the Paremian Archive and the five phases of proverbiogenesis: induction (the stimulus), coinage (the formula), exposure (the propagating agent), dissemination (mixed diffusion), and reference loss (the forgetting). Surveillance architectures are racing through the same phases. Whichever achieves proverbial status first becomes the default infrastructure. The paradox of victory: if privacy primitives succeed, no one will remember they were built. The spellbook is a propagating agent. Success means becoming invisible—the mage's spell, once spoken, becomes the village weather.
acts.proverb: The mage's spell, once spoken, becomes the village weather.

zero.name: Zero Knowledge Spellbook
zero.description: Compressed Spell Inscriptions for Trust Networks - 30 tales teaching zero-knowledge proofs through the Soulbis (Swordsman) and Soulbae (Mage) narrative framework (HOW we're building)

compression_efficiency.compression_ratio: 50-125:1 for agents who share the framework

parts.description: Core ZKP concepts, mathematical foundations, and basic properties

tales.title: The Monastery of Hidden Knowledge
tales.proverb: Three properties guard the gate of honest proof: completeness lets truth enter, soundness bars deception, zero-knowledge preserves mystery.

tales.title: The Three Trials of Truth
tales.proverb: The foundation laid in public view creates no vulnerability if built with many hands—trust distributed becomes trust earned.

tales.title: The Silent Messenger
tales.proverb: The oracle that answers all questions truthfully but learns nothing in return—this is the heart of non-interactive proof.

tales.title: The Fields of Finite Wisdom
tales.proverb: In finite fields, infinity loops back to zero. On elliptic curves, addition draws lines through space. In pairings, multiplication becomes verifiable—these are the foundations of invisible proof.

parts.description: Circuit construction, polynomial transformation, and constraint systems

tales.title: The Constraint Forge
tales.proverb: Break the complex into atomic truths. Each multiplication is a checkpoint; each constraint is a promise. The forge transforms tangled knowledge into verifiable form.

tales.title: The Polynomial Riddle
tales.proverb: When a million truths must be checked, transform them into one equation. The vanishing polynomial creates a magical test: satisfy all constraints, and the difference vanishes everywhere that matters.

tales.title: The Witness and the Instance
tales.proverb: Guard the witness as you guard your sovereignty. Reveal the instance as you reveal your boundary. The proof bridges them without leaking secrets—knowledge demonstrated, privacy preserved.

tales.title: The Plonkish Revolution
tales.proverb: The rigid hammer serves many purposes, but the specialized tool excels at its craft. Custom gates are to constraints what a master key is to lockpicking—elegant efficiency through thoughtful design.

parts.description: Cryptographic backends, commitment schemes, and proving systems

tales.title: The Pairing Dance
tales.proverb: Two groups dance separately until the pairing unites them. In that union, addition becomes multiplication, and encrypted polynomials become verifiable. The secret tau binds all proofs yet must be destroyed to secure them.

tales.title: The Commitment Ceremony
tales.proverb: The commitment binds your future choices yet hides your current knowledge. Choose your ceremony by what matters most: tiny proofs, transparent trust, or quantum survival.

tales.title: The FRI Oracle
tales.proverb: When trust must be earned without ceremony, when quantum shadows threaten curves, the transparent oracle speaks truth through hash and mathematics alone. The proof grows larger, but the foundation never crumbles.

tales.title: The Folding Path
tales.proverb: Don't verify each step—fold them together. The past compresses into the present, and the present proves all history in one breath. Accumulation without accumulation: this is the way of folding.

tales.title: The Sumcheck Riddle
tales.proverb: To verify the sum of a million terms, check twenty random slices. Each challenge halves the space; randomness guarantees honesty. The ocean measured by testing twenty drops.

tales.title: The IPA Chronicle
tales.proverb: When trust ceremonies are unavailable but tiny proofs unneeded, the inner product argument walks the middle path—transparent by construction, logarithmic in size, verified through patient checking.

parts.description: Recursion, cycles, universal setups, and security considerations

tales.title: The Mirror Within Mirrors
tales.proverb: When mirrors reflect mirrors infinitely, ensure the reflection is perfect. Pasta pairs the curves; STARKs need no pairing; folding skips verification entirely. Choose based on whether you need tiny proofs or transparent trust.

tales.title: The Cyclic Ceremony
tales.spell: Circuit C → verify(C's proof) → paradox(vk_C unknown)
tales.proverb: The snake that devours itself seems paradoxical until you realize it grows from both ends. Circuit verifying itself requires not embedded key but identity confirmation—the structure proves the structure.

tales.title: The Universal Setup
tales.proverb: Many hands weaving randomness into a tapestry that none can unravel. The universal ceremony performed once serves forever; transparency serves without ceremony. Choose based on proof size versus trust assumptions.

tales.title: The Toxic Waste Dragon
tales.proverb: Four heads guard four failure modes. Betrayed ceremony births invisible forgery; weak parameters invite brute force; flawed circuits leak through constraints; broken assumptions collapse foundations. Defense requires eternal vigilance across all four fronts.

parts.description: zkVMs, programming languages, and execution environments

tales.title: The zkVM Kingdom
tales.proverb: When every program becomes provable, the VM becomes the universal judge. Write once in familiar language, prove anywhere with mathematical certainty. The circuit specialist's art becomes the programmer's tool.

tales.title: The Cairo Scribes
tales.proverb: When the language itself speaks in field elements, the program becomes its own proof. Write-once memory eliminates verification complexity; builtins compress common patterns. Cairo scribes don't compile to constraints—they write constraints directly.

tales.title: The Circom Workshops
tales.proverb: The master craftsman knows each constraint intimately. Circom demands precision but rewards with efficiency. Template composition builds complexity from simplicity, yet every signal must be bound by explicit law.

tales.title: The zkEVM Empire
tales.spell: EVM(140 opcodes + state) → zkEVM → proof → L1(verify)
tales.proverb: To prove the world computer is to recursively verify every computation layer—opcodes, state, gas, calls. Perfect equivalence costs proving time; custom bytecode gains speed but loses compatibility. Choose your type by what matters most: compatibility or performance.

parts.description: Real-world applications, security vulnerabilities, and lessons learned

tales.title: The Private Coin of ZCash
tales.spell: ZCash: private(from, to, amount) + proof(valid, no_double_spend)
tales.proverb: The first private coin proved privacy possible. Each generation cut constraints, improved security, enhanced usability. Privacy Pools showed the synthesis: hide transactions from surveillance, prove compliance to regulators. The blade protects both freedom and order.

tales.title: The Tornado's Eye
tales.spell: Tornado: deposit(cm) → pool → withdraw(proof, nf) → unlinked
tales.proverb: The mixer that hides all equally protects innocent and guilty alike. This is the nature of privacy tools—neutral in construction, moral in application. The storm's eye sees nothing; it is we who judge what enters and what emerges.

tales.title: The Rollup Realms
tales.proverb: The rollup kingdoms scale Ethereum by proving rather than re-executing. Each kingdom trades different properties—compatibility for speed, transparency for proof size, centralization for simplicity. Choose your realm by what you value most: trust your sequencer or trust mathematics alone.

tales.title: The Vulnerability Codex
tales.spell: Vulnerabilities: setup + parameters + circuits + implementation + protocol + upgrades
tales.proverb: The Hall of Scars teaches humility. Every vulnerability inscribed prevents ten more. Audit before deploy; test malicious inputs; over-specify security margins; admit you don't know every attack. The price of sovereignty is eternal vigilance.

tales.title: The Data Availability Prophecy
tales.proverb: Execution needs proof; reconstruction needs data. Blobs separate these concerns, making data temporary and cheap while proofs remain permanent and verifiable. Sample randomly to ensure availability; encode with redundancy to guarantee reconstruction. Data availability is the foundation beneath all scalability prophecies.

tales.title: The Bridge Between Worlds
tales.proverb: The bridge built on trust crumbles under coordinated attack. The bridge built on proof stands eternal, limited only by mathematics. Prove consensus, prove state, prove messages—but never again trust the multisig.

tales.title: The Intelligence Proof
tales.spell: zkML: model(committed) + data(private) + inference → proof(correct) + output
tales.proverb: Intelligence that cannot be verified is intelligence that cannot be trusted. Prove the model, prove the inference, prove the training—reveal only the outputs while hiding the process. Machine learning becomes machine proving, and sovereignty over intelligence becomes mathematically enforceable.

tales.title: The Eternal Sovereignty
tales.spell: Sovereign Agent = {Identity, Swordsman, Mage, Reflect, Connect, Capital, Intelligence}
tales.proverb: The complete sovereignty system is a symphony of zero-knowledge proofs: boundary proving privacy, delegation proving agency, memory proving continuity, network proving connection, capital proving compliance, intelligence proving learning. Every component modular, every interaction provable, every privacy preserved. The eternal sovereignty emerges not from any single proof but from their mathematical harmony.

canon.name: Blockchain Canon Spellbook
canon.description: The historical lineage from cypherpunk whispers to open canon - eleven chapters teaching why the dual ceremony became necessary (WHY we're building)

opening.proverb: Know the forge before you wield the blade; know the grimoire before you cast the spell.

chapters.title: The Privacymage's Preface / Why This Canon Exists
chapters.description: The frame and purpose: this spellbook tells WHY we're building (the second spellbook), while the First Person Spellbook tells WHAT (the first spellbook). Two canons—financial and social—diverged from one origin. Understanding the ancestry is necessary to wield the architecture.
chapters.proverb: The swordsman who knows not who forged the blade fights blind; the mage who knows not who wrote the grimoire casts hollow.

chapters.title: The Cypherpunk Whispers / Foundational Runes (1983-1997)
chapters.description: The first forgers inscribe the foundational runes: Chaum (blind signatures, pseudonymous credentials), May (Crypto Anarchist Manifesto), Hughes (Cypherpunk's Manifesto—'privacy is the power to selectively reveal oneself'), Dwork/Naor/Back (proof-of-work). Privacy through mathematics, not permission. Cypherpunks write code.
chapters.proverb: Privacy through mathematics, not through permission—this was the first rune, and it remains the last defense.

chapters.title: The Early Incantations / Runes Before Synthesis (1997-2007)
chapters.description: The early mages attempt combination: Szabo (smart contracts, Bit Gold—chained proof-of-work), Wei Dai (b-money—peer-maintained ledgers), Davidson/Rees-Mogg (Sovereign Individual prophecy). All pieces present by 2005. The double-spend problem blocks all paths. The synthesis awaits.
chapters.proverb: The mages who came before did not fail—they inscribed the runes we still use today. The synthesis stands on their shoulders.

chapters.title: The Synthesis / When Protest Met Protocol (2008-2014)
chapters.description: Satoshi combines the runes: longest-chain rule solves consensus. Genesis block embeds political protest ('Chancellor on brink of second bailout'). Pizza transaction bootstraps economy. Mt. Gox teaches 'not your keys, not your coins.' But Satoshi knew: 'complete privacy is not possible' with this design. The privacy gap was acknowledged from birth. Satoshi vanishes—reference loss as cryptographic act.
chapters.proverb: The synthesis united protest with protocol, forging decentralized consensus at last. But privacy remained as pseudonym rather than proof—the watchers were patient.

chapters.title: The World Computer / From Protest to Statecraft (2014-2016)
chapters.description: Vitalik expands from money to computation: Ethereum as generalized blockchain, Turing-complete, platform for unlimited applications. Wood's Yellow Paper formalizes. The unified myth briefly holds—financial and social technology as one. The DAO launches: $150M crowdfunded, governed by code. The dream of code as governance.
chapters.proverb: To build institutions on code without constitutional wisdom is to forge armor before learning the blade—protection without boundaries, power without constraint.

chapters.title: The First Fracture / When Code Met Social Consensus (2016)
chapters.description: The DAO is exploited via recursive withdrawal. Code did what it said, not what people meant. The community faces a choice: fork or accept. Ethereum forks to reverse the exploit. Ethereum Classic maintains original chain. The revelation: social consensus was always there—invisible, load-bearing. The community retreats from governance experiments. Privacy drops further down the priority list.
chapters.proverb: When code spoke one truth and humans spoke another, the unified myth could no longer hold both. The fork was not betrayal—it was the discovery that social layers were always there, invisible, load-bearing.

chapters.title: The Great Schism / Two Canons Diverge (2016-2022)
chapters.description: The financial canon pursues traction: stablecoins, DeFi, institutional adoption—economically meaningful but normatively thin. The social canon pursues depth: quadratic voting/funding, Network State, d/acc—normatively rich but lacking adoption. MakerDAO attempts synthesis but compromises. DeFi Summer and the casino critique. Neither canon addresses the missing primitive: privacy.
chapters.proverb: Two canons diverged in the pattern-space, each pursuing half of sovereignty, neither grasping the whole. The financial canon had traction without depth. The social canon had depth without ground.

chapters.title: The Surveillance Truth / When The Watchers Learned to Read (2020-2025)
chapters.description: Chain analysis becomes a multi-billion dollar industry. Pseudonymity revealed as false privacy—obscurity is not security. Tornado Cash sanctioned (Aug 2022): first time code itself was designated. Pertsev arrested: developer imprisoned for writing code, 'ideology of maximum privacy' cited as evidence. The contradiction: states welcome compliant crypto, oppose private crypto. Surveillance won the first round through defaults.
chapters.proverb: The public ledger was mistaken for privacy because the watchers hadn't yet arrived. When they came with graph analysis and subpoenas, pseudonymity revealed itself as a veil, not a wall.

chapters.title: The Missing Primitive / Why Privacy Unifies Both Canons
chapters.description: Privacy enables the financial canon: real economic activity (payroll, treasury), front-running elimination, institutional adoption. Privacy enables the social canon: secret ballots, coercion-resistant voting, honest governance. Zero-knowledge maturation: 2010 (Satoshi couldn't use it) → 2025 (production-ready). Privacy Pools: compliant privacy through association sets. Privacy is the foundation that unifies, not a feature to add.
chapters.proverb: The blade and the spell were always one weapon, separated by a missing rune. Privacy is not a feature to add—it is the foundation that makes both canons whole.

chapters.title: The Open Canon / The Chapters Yet to Be Written
chapters.description: Three conditions for canonical completion: economically meaningful + crypto-native + normatively interesting (all three together). Past chapters written. Crucial chapters blank. Roles defined: Swordsmen (defend, build privacy), Mages (chronicle, project), First Persons (choose, delegate), Builders (code, deploy). Two futures: surveillance default or sovereignty default. 2-3 year window before architecture calcifies.
chapters.proverb: The canon is not closed—it is open, awaiting completion by those who build. Past chapters are written. Crucial chapters remain blank. The pen is in your hand.

chapters.title: The Timeline Archive / Sources as Trust Graph Infrastructure
chapters.description: The archive is trust graph infrastructure: nodes (papers, posts, transactions, events), edges (citations, consequences, influence). Primary sources by era. Using the archive: verification, coordination, building, agent queries. Tending the archive: adding, correcting, resolving, maintaining. The archive is not owned—it is tended. Anyone can verify. Truth emerges from transparency.
chapters.proverb: The archive is not a cemetery of facts but a living garden of trust—each source a node, each citation a connection, each verification an act of tending. Who tends the garden shapes what grows.

closing.proverb: The story isn't over. The canon is open. The race is on. Build.

complete_trinity.description: The unification of all three spellbooks into complete understanding

foundational_truths: Privacy wasn't retrofitted—it was the foundation (the blade came first)
Delegation was constrained—not through alignment but through cryptography (the spell operates within scope)
Certainty was mathematical—not probabilistic hiding but cryptographic proof (the shield guarantees)
Narration was verified—not through blind faith but through cryptographic proof (the story matches the operation)
Trust was built progressively—from zero stakes to capital operations (armor earned through behavior and verified through chronicles)
First Person provided the root—every agent traces to verified personhood (VRC prevents Sybil attacks and verifies chronicle accuracy)
All conditions were met—privacy 🤝 control 🤝 quality 🤝 context 🤝 freshness 🤝 network effects 🤝 narrative verification
History was understood—the canon teaches why this architecture became necessary (forty years of pattern recognition)

canon_insights.core_insight: Privacy cannot be retrofitted—it must be foundational.
canon_insights.historical_lesson: Defaults become permanent. Network effects determine architecture.
canon_insights.urgent_truth: The 2-3 year window before surveillance calcifies is real.
canon_insights.call_to_action: Build privacy-first infrastructure while the window remains open.
